**What we’re adding (safety first):** | Feature | Safety parts we’ll build in | |---------|-----------------------------| | Email‑only log‑in (magic link or code) | • Uses a proven auth service (Supabase Auth, Clerk, Firebase Auth, etc.) so you don’t write password logic.
• Site URL and redirect URLs are checked in the auth‑service settings.
• Email is sent through your own SMTP provider or a third‑party service you control – the built‑in “test” server only sends a few emails an hour.
• No user‑visible secrets: the magic‑link code is time‑bounded and delivered only to the user’s inbox.
• Secret keys stay on the server (in your `.env` or platform secrets). | **Next steps – quick starter questions** 1. Which auth provider do you already have (or want to set up) – Supabase Auth, Clerk, Firebase Auth, Auth0, etc.? 2. Do you already have an SMTP or transactional‑email service (e.g. SendGrid, Postmark, Mailgun) connected, or would you like a simple integration guide? 3. Is the site already deployed (e.g. on Vercel, Netlify, Replit) so we can set the allowed redirect URLs, or does it need a new deployment step? Once you answer, we’ll: 1. Create a *save point* (git commit or zip). 2. Add the auth configuration in the dev environment. 3. Add a protected route that only signed‑in users can see. 4. Update the front‑end with a simple “Sign in with email” button. 5. Verify the email is sent and the link works. 6. Push the changes to your live environment. **Safety checklist we’ll cover in this feature** - **Keys secret** – all API keys in `.env`, never in browser code. - **Data locked to its owner** – once signed in, the user only sees their own data (RLS rules if you have a database). - **Spending caps** – we’ll enable a short‑term rate limit on email sends so one user can’t spam the service. - **Save point before each change** – every edit is committed with a clear message like `feat: add email‑only login`. Let me know your answers to the questions above, and we’ll start building!
